children: Meta Platforms
has thrown its hat into the $30T

, its standalone AI agent that lets users automate tasks and turn “long-term goals into action plans.” And while Muse’s ability to access personal data to complete tasks raises privacy concerns, Meta runs the agent on a separate, secure virtual machine, helping ensure private data remains isolated and is not shared across platforms.
Muse also features an intuitive interface that lowers the learning curve for users while allowing them to opt in to the specific apps and services Muse can access and interact with.
With a broad reach across platforms and future opportunities for monetization, Wall Street analysts view Meta’s Muse as a worthy rival to Google’s
Gemini and Anthropic's
Claude .

“Meta’s distribution and data advantage give Muse an advantage on day one. If Muse can build a monthly (and ideally, daily or weekly) audience in the hundreds of millions over the coming months, we believe this would be deemed a success,” KeyBanc analyst Justin Patterson writes in a note to clients.

“As with other Meta apps, we view engagement as the initial barometer of success with monetization following over time,” Patterson adds, noting that the market underestimates Meta’s AI positioning and product cycle.
With the integration of other monetizable apps and personalized datasets, Meta
has an “edge to create a more personalized agent with new monetizable behaviors,” notes Morgan Stanley’s Brian Nowak, which will help offset Meta’s huge AI investments and free cash flow compression.
For investors, Muse's launch not only justifies Meta’s
multi-billion dollar AI budget but also proves the company can successfully challenge the AI dominance of startups and rivals.
“Investors are misunderstanding AI's positive impact on Meta’s business,” said
adding that “this condition is creating a discount (and opportunity) here.”

“AI investments drive increased engagement and lead to new products and services, which supports outsized monetization and revenue growth,” writes Morgan Stanley’s Nowak. “We think Meta’s 'year of efficiency’ is more than just a 365-day change but rather a structural and cultural pivot to operate leaner and with a greater focus on investor returns.”

KeyBanc’s Patterson agrees that AI investments will improve Meta’s core business and open up new opportunities and show itself as a business with more durability to achieve 20% revenue growth over the medium term.

“Our bull case assumes Meta’s revenue grows in the mid- to high-20% range with moderating investment levels. In this scenario, we believe Meta can trade at a 25x 2028E price/earnings,” Patterson writes.

The bullish view among analysts is that if Meta can turn its massive user base, proprietary data, and growing AI capabilities into sustained engagement, the billions being spent on AI could ultimately prove to be an investment in the company’s next phase of growth rather than a drag on returns.

title: Meta's Muse gives its AI ambitions a new monetization engine
